question: q-128452

original_content.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
original_content.problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}$ at $t=-1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨8\sqrt{3-t},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t)⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\,\pi {t}^{2},\,1-{t}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
original_content.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)-{g}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\sqrt{3-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-t}},\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,\frac{1}{t}⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\pi {t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-1,\,2\pi t,\,-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(-1)-g(-1))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(-1)-{g}^{′}(-1) \\  & =2⟨-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-(-1)}},\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi ),\,\frac{1}{(-1)}⟩-⟨2(-1)-1,\,2\pi (-1),\,-2(-1)⟩ \\  & =2⟨-2,-\pi ,-1⟩-⟨-3,-2\pi ,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-2\pi ,-2⟩-⟨-3,-2\pi ,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.knowledge_point: Using the Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
corrected_content.problem:
Find the value of $(2f(t)-g(t))^{′}$ at $t=-1,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨8\sqrt{3-t},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,\ln|2t|⟩, \\ g(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\,\pi {t}^{2},\,1-{t}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Since $t=-1$ lies in an open interval where $t<0$ and $3-t>0$, all components are differentiable there. In particular, $\ln|2t|=\ln(-2t)$ near $t=-1$, so its derivative is $1/t$.

Differentiate each vector component:

$$
\mathbf f'(t)=\left\langle-\frac{4}{\sqrt{3-t}},\pi\cos(\pi t),\frac1t\right\rangle,
\qquad
\mathbf g'(t)=\langle 2t-1,2\pi t,-2t\rangle.
$$

The sum and constant multiple rules give

$$
(2\mathbf f-\mathbf g)'(t)=2\mathbf f'(t)-\mathbf g'(t).
$$

At $t=-1$,

$$
\mathbf f'(-1)=\langle-2,-\pi,-1\rangle,
\qquad
\mathbf g'(-1)=\langle-3,-2\pi,2\rangle.
$$

Therefore,

$$
(2\mathbf f-\mathbf g)'(-1)
=2\langle-2,-\pi,-1\rangle-\langle-3,-2\pi,2\rangle
=\boxed{\langle-1,0,-4\rangle}.
$$

rationale: The original real-valued function uses ln(2t), undefined at the requested t=-1. Its derivative there therefore does not exist. The site accepts its formal derivative <-1,0,-4>. The explicitly authorized local repair replaces ln(2t) by ln|2t|, making that result valid on a neighborhood of -1.
